To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resistance training is associated with higher HRQoL (both mental and physical health) and lower depression symptoms, regardless of the amount of sedentary behavior.

(i) resistance training, regardless of level of sedentary behavior, was positively associated with mental health, physical health and self-esteem, and negatively associated with depression; (ii) resistance training was associated with higher levels of satisfaction with life; and (iii) resistance training and sedentariness were both associated with higher anxiety.
